page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL4 is an x86_64 architecture cloud server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 20 shared vCPUs paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.8 GB per vCPU. The server is equipped with two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, meaning storage must be provisioned externally. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

The shared CPU allocation model presents a performance tradeoff, as CPU resources are shared with other tenants, which may introduce processing variability during sustained compute-heavy operations. However, the presence of dual dedicated NVIDIA L4 GPUs offsets this for parallelizable workloads, offering high resource density for graphics, video processing, and machine learning. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this configuration provides a substantial memory footprint and modern GPU acceleration without the premium cost of dedicated high-end enterprise GPU nodes.

This server is designed for workloads that require significant GPU acceleration and large memory capacity but do not demand constant, dedicated CPU performance. Suitable use cases include machine learning inference, medium-scale AI model training, video transcoding, 3D rendering, and data analytics pipelines that leverage GPU acceleration.
